newsitem.title: UK: Sterling firm in Europe, banks on higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Sterling firm in Europe, banks on higher rates.

text.p: Sterling pushed higher above 3.0 marks and $1.63 in Europe, bolstered as market expectations for a rate hike next week intensified, said traders.
Against the mark, sterling was at 3.0060/70 at 1000 GMT, up over 1-1/2 pfennig from 2.9890/00 in late Europe on Wednesday. Cable was at $1.6378/88 and up near a cent from $1.6300/10.

Traders said an already buoyant pound, recovering after a slump earlier this week, got a leg-up after UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said a Times interview he had no plans for a special autumn budget to brake consumer spending. He also hinted at no intervention on markets to stem the pound's gains.

When asked about intervention if the pound maintained its strength, he said: "What I am going to do is keep my eye on what matters even more to the industry, and that is that we do not return to instability."

Traders said Brown's comments, ruling out tax hikes as a way to restrict consumer demand, and robust July housing figures released have enhanced chances of rate rises at the Bank of England's policy meeting next week.
"It all points to higher rates next week...The pound's downside now looks limited," said a senior trader at a U.S. bank.
A Reuters poll of economists showed on Thursday that British interest rates are likely to rise next week for the fourth time in as many months in order to stem inflation.
Sixteen of the 23 London-based economists surveyed said the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee (MCP) would raise base rates by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent when it meets on August 6 and 7.
For sterling, this means higher ground, said analysts.
"The risk is still on the upside, essentially because the risk for short-rates are on the upside," said Adam Cole, analyst at HSBC James Capel.

And a buoyant sterling could even re-visit its high of 3.0878 marks, its highest since August 1989, touched last week. "We could see sterling getting back up to 3.09/3.10 against the deutschmark and that is about as far as I see it going," said Cole.
The pound slid from a high of 3.0627 marks on Monday to lows of 2.9735 marks on Tuesday.
But analysts said that while the move was a correction to an overdone market, longer term the pound would head lower as it looked for base rates to peak.
